Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA), the electric-vehicle and AI-robotics company, entered a closely watched California discrimination trial Monday tied to allegations involving its Fremont factory. Shares gained approximately 3% to $375.17, showing investors were looking past the immediate legal headline as trading remained firmly positive.

California alleges Black workers faced harassment, unequal pay and fewer opportunities for promotion at the plant. Tesla denies wrongdoing, says discrimination is prohibited under its policies and has said employees responsible for misconduct have been dismissed. Judge Peter Borkon has scheduled the bench trial to run through October 30, meaning the legal issue could remain in the background for Tesla investors for several weeks.

Tesla Gains 3% as Fremont Bias Claims Reach Trial · us.finance.gurufocus

The valuation picture adds another layer. Tesla's $375.17 share price sits 12.33% above its GF Value estimate of $333.99, showing the market is already assigning the company a meaningful premium over GuruFocus' estimate of fair value. California law does not impose a cap on potential damages, but neither liability nor any financial award has been determined. For shareholders, the bigger question is whether the proceedings ultimately remain a contained legal expense or expose broader weaknesses in workplace oversight, employee retention and operating controls at one of Tesla's most important manufacturing sites.

title: Tesla Stock Rises After Major Self-Driving Win in Europe
detail:
Tesla Stock Rises After Major Self-Driving Win in Europe
Nauman Khan
Mon, September 21, 2026 at 1:50 PM CDT 1 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Tesla (TSLA) moved higher Monday after the Czech Republic granted provisional approval for the automaker's Full Self-Driving system, clearing the way for a rollout in the country.

The decision marks a shift from the country's earlier reservations about the technology. Czech authorities said additional European operating data, experience from other markets, and monitoring measures helped address concerns tied to speed-limit compliance and driver supervision.

Tesla said on X that deployment of the system in the Czech Republic is expected to begin soon. The approval follows a similar authorization by Dutch regulator RDW earlier this year and adds to a growing list of European countries allowing the software under provisional frameworks.

Full Self-Driving is an advanced driver-assistance system that can handle steering, braking, and acceleration while requiring drivers to remain attentive and ready to take control. Tesla has been seeking broader acceptance of the technology across Europe as regulators evaluate its safety and performance.

Tesla shares climbed about 2.7% in recent trading.

title: Tesla Heads Into High-Stakes California Court Fight
detail:
Tesla Heads Into High-Stakes California Court Fight
Moz Farooque ACCA
Mon, September 21, 2026 at 1:27 PM CDT 2 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) is heading into a major California civil-rights trial that could add another layer of legal risk for the electric-vehicle maker. The California Civil Rights Department's lawsuit, filed in 2022 on behalf of thousands of Black workers, alleges widespread racial harassment, discrimination and retaliation at Tesla's Fremont factory. For investors, the case matters less because of any single potential fine and more because it adds to an already substantial legal and regulatory overhang around the company.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

TSLA GF Value chart

The state agency alleges Black employees were subjected to racial slurs, racist graffiti and drawings of nooses and swastikas across the Fremont plant.

It also claims Black workers were concentrated in lower-paying jobs, paid less than white colleagues and faced harsher treatment after complaining about workplace conditions. The agency alleges Tesla knew about the conduct but failed to adequately prevent or stop it.

Tesla has rejected the allegations and has said it does not tolerate discrimination.

The case now moves before Superior Court Judge Peter Borkon, with proceedings expected to extend into late October. Tesla could face millions of dollars in damages if it loses.

The litigation has already survived an important challenge. In May, Alameda County Superior Court rejected Tesla's attempt to dismiss the case, finding factual disputes that should be resolved at trial.

Still, Tesla has scored some legal victories. Borkon previously ruled that Black workers pursuing a separate case could not proceed as a class after their lawyers failed to produce enough representative employees. Tesla has also settled claims with some individual workers while continuing to face a separate discrimination lawsuit from the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.

Investor Takeaway

The immediate financial exposure from this trial is unlikely to rival Tesla's core earnings drivers, but investors should watch for any ruling that establishes broader liability or encourages additional claims. Potential damages, further settlements and the separate federal discrimination case could compound the company's legal costs. More importantly, repeated workplace litigation can become a governance and reputational issue if it begins affecting recruiting, retention or regulatory scrutiny. The key near-term catalyst is the trial outcome and whether the court narrows or expands Tesla's potential liability.

title: TSLA, RUN Stocks In Focus — 580 MW Heat-Wave Battery Drop Lifts Tesla And Sunrun Despite 2026 Losses
detail:
TSLA, RUN Stocks In Focus — 580 MW Heat-Wave Battery Drop Lifts Tesla And Sunrun Despite 2026 Losses
Anan Ashraf
Mon, September 21, 2026 at 12:35 PM CDT 2 min read
RUN
TSLA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

More than 140,000 household batteries discharged for three evening hours on Sept. 9, peaking above 580 megawatts—enough, the companies said, to cover every home in Sacramento County at peak.

About 110,000 Tesla Powerwalls supplied 517 megawatts; Sunrun owns or runs 55% of those units.

Sunrun CEO Mary Powell said the home-battery network now rivals many traditional backup plants.

Sunrun (RUN) and Tesla (TSLA) said on Monday that more than 140,000 household batteries sent power into California's grid on the evening of Sept. 9, when a heat wave lifted demand and wholesale prices.

The companies reported a peak of more than 580 megawatts over a three-hour window and described the coordinated discharge as the biggest residential virtual-power-plant event they have recorded.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

State officials and utilities asked the companies to tap customer batteries for three hours so the grid had extra supply and prices could ease. About 110,000 Tesla Powerwall batteries supplied 517 megawatts. Sunrun owns or runs 55% of those units. Sunrun also used more than 30,000 batteries from other makers, adding 63 megawatts.

Tesla rose about 2.4% on Monday to near $373 amid a broader market rally. Sunrun gained about 4% to about $8.87.

A Second Night In Southern California

The next evening, Southern California Edison asked for another three-hour release. The companies said they delivered more than 140 megawatts. If both nights had overlapped, they estimated more than 720 megawatts.

Sunrun CEO Mary Powell said the home-battery network now rivals many traditional backup plants and can lower costs even for people who never bought a battery.

Other News Impacting The Stocks

On Monday, the Czech Republic provisionally cleared Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving software, the seventh European Union country to do so. Tesla said a local rollout would start soon. Drivers must still stay alert; the system is not fully self-driving.

Goldman Sachs also cut its Sunrun price target to $13 from $15 and kept a 'Buy' rating. The fresh price target still implies a potential upside of about 52% from the stock's last close.

How Did Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA was extremely bearish at the time of writing, while sentiment around RUN stayed at bearish levels.

TSLA stock has fallen 17% this year, while RUN has lost 52%.
